options.text: In the PI Interface, before data is sent to the Data Archive
In the Snapshot Subsystem, before data is written to the archive
In the Archive Subsystem write cache
In PI Vision, when a trend is drawn

explanation: Exception is a deadband filter applied only by PI Interfaces, before data reaches the snapshot, which saves network bandwidth. The Snapshot Subsystem applies compression, not exception.

prompt: A tag has Compressing = 1 and CompDev = 0. Its value stays at exactly 42.0 for an hour. What is archived?

options.text: Every snapshot event, because a deviation of 0 keeps everything
The repeated identical values are dropped; set Compressing = 0 to store every event
Nothing at all until CompMin elapses
Only the first event, and CompMax is ignored

explanation: With compression on, CompDev = 0 still drops flat-lined (identical) values; the line between archived points reproduces them exactly. To archive every snapshot event, turn compression off with Compressing = 0. CompMax still forces an archived value after its time limit.

prompt: An instrument's precision is ±0.4 in the tag's engineering units. Following AVEVA's rule of thumb, which settings are a sensible start?

options.text: CompDev 0.4, ExcDev 0.2
CompDev 0.2, ExcDev 0.4
CompDev 0.8, ExcDev 0.4
CompDev 0, ExcDev 0

explanation: The rule of thumb is CompDev no larger than the instrument precision and ExcDev half of CompDev. Option b reverses them, option c makes CompDev wider than the instrument can resolve, and option d keeps noise.

prompt: Which statement about ExcMin is correct?

options.text: It forces the interface to send a value at least every ExcMin seconds
It blocks values that arrive sooner than ExcMin after the last reported value, and never forces a value to be sent
It is the minimum deviation, in engineering units, for a value to be sent
It controls how long the archive keeps a value

explanation: ExcMin only blocks values and is typically 0. ExcMax is the time limit that forces a value through, and ExcDev is the deviation deadband.

prompt: Match each point attribute to its default value for a new point.
explanation: New points are filtered by default: ExcDevPercent 0.1, ExcMax 600 s (10 minutes), CompDevPercent 0.2 and CompMax 28800 s (8 hours).

prompt: Which of these bypass the compression test? Select all that apply.

options.text: Out-of-order data
Data backfilled before the current snapshot
A new value that arrives after CompMax has elapsed
Every value from an interface with ExcDev = 0

explanation: Out-of-order data and data backfilled before the snapshot go straight to the archive. A value after CompMax is still evaluated by the snapshot; it is archived because the time limit is reached. ExcDev = 0 only affects exception at the interface.

prompt: Put the steps a new reading passes through in order, from the source to disk.

items.text: PI Buffer Subsystem forwards the event
Snapshot Subsystem applies the compression test
Archive Subsystem writes it to an archive file

explanation: Exception runs at the interface, the buffer forwards to the server, the Snapshot Subsystem applies compression and passes archive-worthy events to the event queue, and the Archive Subsystem writes them to the archive files.

scenario: A totaliser tag often sits at the same value for hours. The reporting team needs one archived value every 60 seconds, even when nothing changes. Compression is on with default settings.
prompt: Which change meets the requirement with the least side effect?

options.text: Set CompDev to 0
Set CompMax to 60
Set ExcMin to 60
Set CompMin to 60

explanation: CompMax = 60 archives the next event once 60 seconds have passed since the last archived one, so a value is kept each minute. CompDev = 0 still drops identical values, ExcMin only blocks values, and CompMin delays archiving.

prompt: Which point attribute, set to 0, makes the Data Archive archive every snapshot event for that point?
explanation: Compressing = 0 turns compression off for the point, so every snapshot event is archived. CompDev = 0 is not the same: identical values are still dropped.

scenario: A tag has ExcDev 70 and CompDev 140 with default ExcMax and CompMax. An engineer finds archived values that differ from the previous archived value by only 5 units, roughly eight hours apart.
prompt: What is the most likely explanation?

options.text: Compression is broken and the archive needs reprocessing
The time limits (ExcMax and CompMax) forced the values through
ExcMin is set too high
The interface ignores ExcDev when CompDev is set

explanation: ExcMax (600 s by default) forces a value to be sent and CompMax (28800 s, 8 hours) forces one to be archived even when it is inside the deadband. Small changes eight hours apart are the expected signature of CompMax.
